key_facts: NAR pending home sales index fell 7.3% month-on-month in September and was down 11.3% year-on-year, hitting an all-time low in records dating to 2001; Wall Street consensus expected a 0.4% decline.

Privately owned housing starts fell at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 5.2% in September versus expectations of a 0.4% decline; building permits fell 0.2% against a consensus 2% gain. Single-family permits totaled 845,000, down 4% from August and the lowest since 2023.

The 30-year mortgage rate was above 7% for most of September and ended the month around 7.6% per Mortgage News Daily; the Fed is weighing further rate hikes, with futures implying a strong chance of a quarter-point hike in December and another in March 2027, while markets expect a hold at next week's meeting.

Wholesale final demand goods prices rose 2.6%, the fastest pace in the BLS series dating to December 2009; Goldman Sachs forecasts residential investment declines of 2.5%, 4% and 1% over the coming three quarters and single-family starts of 875,000 in 2027.
importance_reason: Sharp housing contraction (record-low pending sales, weak starts) coinciding with rising mortgage rates and possible further Fed hikes creates a systemic policy-and-markets dilemma.
market_link: Higher mortgage rates and possible Fed hikes weigh on housing-linked equities, homebuilders and bond yields; a hawkish Fed path is also a factor for USD and rate-sensitive assets.

key_facts: The UK government is expected to announce a decision on whether to approve the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea, reportedly on Wednesday morning, with the Energy Secretary expected to address MPs in the afternoon.
Westminster widely believes Jackdaw will be approved, while a decision on the Rosebank oil field off Shetland is not expected yet. The decisions have been delayed for several months.

Jackdaw is about 150 miles (241.4 km) east of Aberdeen and its operators say it could be connected to the UK network within months. Rosebank is about 80 miles (128.7 km) north-west of Shetland and is Britain's largest untapped oil field.

The Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that Rosebank and Jackdaw were unlawfully approved because the government had not considered the climate impact of burning the extracted oil and gas. Licences were granted in 2022 and 2023 under the Conservative government.

Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged no new North Sea oil and gas licences but to honour existing ones such as Jackdaw. Industry bodies argue the fields will bring jobs and energy security, while environmentalists oppose further drilling.
importance_reason: Значимое национальное энергетическое решение с политическим и климатическим измерением, но без прямого шока для мировых рынков.
market_link: Одобрение добычи может повлиять на британский газовый баланс и цены на газ в Великобритании; прямой эффект на мировые котировки нефти и газа неочевиден.
